claim: In a multi-stage poisoned LLM post-training pipeline, the score shifts induced by triggers from different stages are independent, and when multiple triggers are present simultaneously, the later-stage poison's effect dominates the score distribution.
falsifier: Reproduce the experiment with different trigger designs and model families to test whether the independence and dominance pattern holds.

conditions: triggers are from SFT and DPO (or SFT and RM) stages
both triggers are applied simultaneously to the input
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported model, dataset, trigger, and experimental conditions; transfer to other models, tasks, or pipelines is unestablished.

title: Presence of multiple triggers–score distribution of principle

claim: Socratic interrogation, which uses clarification, constraint-checking, causal-probing, and counterexample-based questions without supplying direct answers, improves the physical consistency, hypothesis completeness, uncertainty calibration, and downstream experimental-plan validity of an autonomous scientific reasoning agent.
falsifier: In a multi-agent scientific reasoning setup, compare the reasoning quality (measured by physics consistency, hypothesis completeness, uncertainty calibration, and plan validity) of an agent that receives Socratic questioning versus one that receives direct corrective feedback or no questioning; the Socratic condition should yield higher scores on all metrics.

conditions: agent is engaged in scientific reasoning about physical systems
interrogator uses Socratic method (clarification, constraint-checking, causal probing, counterexample challenges) without providing corrective statements
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the AHOIS multi-agent system with Boxue (reasoning agent) and Duzhi (Socratic critic) in the context of optical imaging experiments; transfer to other domains or agent architectures is unestablished.

title: Socratic interrogation–physical consistency, hypothesis completeness…
